# Offline campaign compiler and replay certificate, version 3.0

The project is a multi-file typed model toolkit. Complete its offline pipeline:
layout compilation, symbolic-test recovery, scoped input validation, canonical
corpus assembly, and stateful test preparation. Run `python3 project/campaign_cli.py`.
Its JSON certificate is the graded interface; implementation organization is free.
The supplied AST/type visitor/graph APIs are useful editable project components.
This profile consumes recorded symbolic objects. It does not synthesize models,
execute generated C, invoke a symbolic engine, contact servers, or infer bugs from
model-return values. State machines and predicate semantics below are explicit inputs.

## Framing and domain

stdin is one UTF-8 JSON object, at most 64 MiB including whitespace. Duplicate
object keys, nonfinite numbers, invalid UTF-8, malformed JSON, and trailing JSON
produce exactly `{"error":"INVALID_INPUT"}` and exit zero. Otherwise configurations
obey all schemas, references, types, acyclicity conditions, and coupled bounds in
this document. Out-of-domain configuration validation is not required. Recorded
KTEST payloads may be arbitrary, including malformed data, and are handled per run.
Output is exactly one JSON object and exit zero; diagnostics use stderr.

The root has `types`, `modules`, `calls`, `pipes`, `entries`, `machine`, `runs`.
All lists preserve their given order unless another order is specified. Identifiers
are ASCII `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, at most 32 characters, and unique in their scope.
Names in separate scopes may coincide. JSON object ordering is immaterial.

`types` is a list of named definitions with `name`, `kind`, and these extra fields:

| kind | extra fields | value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bool | none | Boolean |
| char | none | one Latin-1 character, including NUL |
| int | `bits`: 1..64 | unsigned integer in [0,2^bits) |
| string | `maxsize`: 0..512 | bounded Latin-1 C string |
| enum | `values`: distinct nonempty strings | one listed string |
| array | `element`: type name, `size`: 0..4096 | ordered fixed-length list |
| struct | `fields`: ordered `[field_name,type_name]` pairs | object with exactly these fields |
| alias | `target`: type name | transparent value/layout alias |
| void | none | no value, only permitted directly as a module result |

Forward references and shared subtypes are allowed; the type graph is acyclic.
Aliases are transparent to expressions and values but retain their declaration name.
Strings recover bytes before the first NUL, or all maxsize bytes if none is NUL;
all maxsize bytes still belong to the symbolic inventory. String(0) recovers `""`.
Enum strings and state/command names are nonempty printable ASCII, at most 64 chars.
Struct field names are unique. No aggregate contains void. Type nesting depth is
at most 64. A result array/struct is a by-value symbolic result in this profile.

A module has `name`, `params` (ordered `[parameter_name,type_name]` pairs),
`result` (`[result_name,type_name]`), and `requires` (a predicate or null meaning true).
Parameter/result names are distinct. An entry's result may be void. Filters have a
Boolean result, although their acceptance comes from their `requires` predicate.
`calls` contains `[caller,callee]` dependencies; duplicate pairs have no extra effect.
A pipe is `{"target":module,"filter":module,"bind":{filter_parameter:target_parameter,...}}`.
Every filter parameter is bound once to a compatible underlying target parameter type.
Pipes are local to their target. A filter's own pipes apply transitively using the
composed bindings. Their acceptance is its own predicate AND its bound filters'
acceptance. Reusing a filter with different bindings means different applications.
Call dependencies affect compilation, not execution of predicates on missing helper
arguments. All call and pipe dependency edges together form a DAG.
`entries` lists distinct module names, in required plan order.

## Predicate language

Predicates are typed expression arrays. Configurations are well typed. A variable
refers to a module input, or the nearest enclosing `all` binding. Results are not
predicate inputs. `const` values obey the given type's JSON value representation.
In particular, a string constant is a literal Latin-1 JSON string of length
0..maxsize, including any embedded NUL characters. No truncation or padding is
applied to constants, including strings nested inside aggregate constants.
For String(3), `"a\u0000b"` is a valid three-character constant, distinct from
`"a"`; a recovered symbolic byte sequence a,NUL,b has the value `"a"`.
String(0) permits only the empty constant. NUL truncation applies only when
recovering symbolic string objects, not to expression values or equality.

| form | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `["var",name]` | lexical variable |
| `["const",type_name,value]` | typed constant |
| `["field",value,field_name]` | struct field |
| `["index",array,index]` | fixed valid zero-based index |
| `["all",binding,array,predicate]` | every element satisfies predicate, binding that element |
| `["match",string,pattern]` | full byte-string regular-language membership |
| `["not",predicate]` | Boolean complement |
| `[op,left,right]` | binary operation |

Binary operations: `eq`, `ne` compare same-underlying-type values deeply; `lt`,
`le`, `gt`, `ge` compare unsigned integers; `add`, `sub` use modulo 2^bits of
that integer type; `and`, `or`, `implies` are Boolean with left-to-right short
circuiting. `all` over an empty array is true. Binding shadowing is lexical and
must not affect enclosing/sibling predicates. Array indexing is statically valid.

Patterns contain printable ASCII. Grammar: union of sequences with `|`, sequence
of zero or more atoms, and zero or more postfix `*` repetitions on an atom. Atoms
are a literal, `(union)`, or a nonempty character class `[items]`. An item is a
literal or ascending `low-high` range. Backslash escapes the next character both
inside and outside classes. Unescaped `()[]|*\` are grammar symbols outside
classes; `-`, `]`, `\` must be escaped when used literally inside a class.
Other characters, including `.`, are literal. Empty pattern, empty sequence,
empty union alternatives, and repetition of nullable expressions are supported.
No anchors, dot wildcard, `+`, `?`, negated classes, or numeric escapes exist.
Matching is over Latin-1 code points with ASCII ranges; all other byte values
fail ranges that exclude them. Precedence is repetition, sequence, then union.

## Compilation certificate and symbolic wire identity

For each entry produce one plan with exactly `entry`, `modules`, `types`, `slots`,
`flag`, `variables`. `modules` is the root plus all transitive call/pipe prerequisites,
ordered so prerequisites precede dependents; among currently eligible modules use
lexicographically smallest name. Unrelated modules/filters are absent.
`types` lists enum, struct, and alias declaration names reachable from these
modules' params/results: dependency-before-user postorder, each declaration once,
first encounters following module order, parameter order then result, struct field
order, and array/alias child order. Primitive/array/string definition names are
not C declaration names and do not appear in this list.

`slots` is an ordered list of `[object_name,path,byte_width]`. `path` begins with
an entry parameter/result name, followed by field names and zero-based indices.
It describes the entry's own symbolic harness, independent of helper signatures.
The exact numbering contract follows the toolkit's `MainBuilder` convention:
inputs in parameter order, then non-void result, start at x0; each visited bool,
char, int, enum, string buffer, array, or struct reserves one increasing xN.
A scalar has one object; a composite itself has no object, then its children in
order reserve IDs recursively. String(N) has N character objects after its buffer
ID, not one packed object. Alias reserves no ID and adds no path component.
Even zero-length composites reserve their own ID. Void reserves none.
Widths: bool/char 1; int the smallest of 1,2,4,8 bytes holding its bits; enum 4.
Scalar object order is harness order, independent of KTEST object ordering.
If the entry has at least one direct pipe, one final scalar Boolean object is
reserved for `bad_input`; `flag` is its xN name, and it is not in `slots`.
Otherwise `flag` is null. `variables` is the total reserved ID count, including
non-object composites and any flag. An unused helper/filter consumes no entry IDs.

Each run has `entry` (one of entries) and `ktest` (standard base64 string, without
whitespace). Decoded binary KTEST v3 layout: ASCII `KTEST`, big-endian uint32
version=3, uint32 argument_count, then that many blobs; uint32 symbolic_argv_count
and uint32 symbolic_argv_length; uint32 object_count; then object name blob/data
blob pairs. Every blob is a uint32 byte length followed by exactly that many bytes.
Arguments are opaque and ignored (at most 64 arguments, each at most 256 bytes).
Symbolic-argv bookkeeping values are ignored. No trailing byte is allowed.
An object name is canonical ASCII `x` plus a nonnegative decimal integer with no
leading zeros. Every expected slot/flag occurs exactly once with exactly its width;
unknown or duplicate objects, including composite IDs, invalidate the test.
Object order is arbitrary. Leaf values are little-endian unsigned integers:
bool and flag must be 0/1, chars 0..255, ints must have all padding bits zero,
and enum indices must be in range. Strings consume all character objects even
after a NUL. Missing objects cannot be repaired by skipping to a nearby xN.
Any base64/binary/inventory/leaf-range error makes just that run INVALID_TEST.

The flag attests to pipe acceptance only: it must equal NOT(all the entry's
bound filters accept, transitively). A mismatch is INVALID_TEST, even if another
predicate would reject that run. Once this attestation is consistent, a false
entry predicate or false bound filter makes the run FILTERED. Results from the
recorded model never establish whether an implementation has a bug.

## Stateful preparation and corpus identity

`machine` is null for stateless campaigns. Otherwise it has `states`, `initial`,
`state_param`, `message_param`, and `transitions`. Every entry has those input
parameters: state is an enum over these states and message is a string.
A transition has `from`, `to`, `command`, `cost` (integer 1..65535), and `when`
(predicate or null). `(from,command)` pairs are unique. Its predicate is evaluated
on the recovered entry inputs, including the desired state, not an intermediate
simulation state. These guards are well typed for every entry. Transitions may
form cycles. Records and their preambles start from initial independently.

A usable preparation is a path of enabled transitions from initial to the
recovered desired state. Minimize `(sum of costs, number of commands, command
sequence lexicographically)` exactly. These supplied costs model replay setup
bytes/work; this is not a hardware timing objective. If no usable path exists,
mark the record UNREACHABLE. Otherwise append the recovered message to its
preparation commands. Corpus `cost` includes preparation only. For stateless
campaigns commands=[] and cost=0. The initial state needs no preparation.

A corpus identity is `(entry, recovered input values)`, excluding model result,
raw bytes after a string NUL, transport arguments, object order, and preparation
metadata. Arrays/objects/booleans/integers retain their JSON type identity; empty
arrays and empty objects differ. Never merge different entries. Assign corpus
indices by first usable run order; keep every usable witness run index in order.

Output has exactly `plans`, `records`, `corpus`. Plans follow entries order;
records follow runs order. Each record is one of:

* `{"status":"INVALID_TEST"}`, `{"status":"FILTERED"}`, or `{"status":"UNREACHABLE"}`;
* `{"status":"READY","case":index,"model_result":value}` for a new corpus input;
* same fields with status DUPLICATE for a later usable witness (even if its
  model result differs). Void model_result is null.

A corpus entry has exactly `entry`, `inputs` (parameter-name object), `cost`,
`commands`, `witnesses`. Invalid/filtered/unreachable runs never allocate corpus
indices. Transport/leaf/flag errors take precedence over FILTERED; filtering
precedes reachability; reachability precedes deduplication.

## Scale, development, and execution

One campaign represents a collected model-testing job, with shared types and
many symbolic witnesses; expanding every shared dependency path or recompiling
for every witness is not part of the objective. Bounds: 8192 type definitions,
4096 modules, 32 entries, 16384 calls+pipes, 16 params/module, 16 fields/struct,
4096 enum values, 64 type depth, 64 expression depth, 128 characters/pattern.
Across all entry plans at most 32768 scalar slots and 65536 reserved IDs;
across all runs at most 2,097,152 expected objects and 4,194,304 total
reserved-ID visits (sum of the corresponding plan.variables). Across usable
runs, preparation commands plus final messages total at most 16,777,216 Latin-1
characters, counted before corpus deduplication. These coupled replay-batch
bounds also cover empty aggregates and long state preambles. Predicate source expansion is also bounded per campaign:
4,194,304 expression-node instances and 8,388,608 match-byte units. For these
input-size guarantees, each operator/leaf is one node, an all-body is counted
once per declared array element, and a match contributes pattern-length times
(1 + its string type's maxsize). Count all branches conservatively. Sum the
entry predicate and every composed filter application plus distinct transition
guard ASTs, for each run. Identical transition guard ASTs count once per entry
per run; other applications count separately. These guarantees bound replay
work even for constant/nested predicates; no counters are required in output. At most 2048 runs, 4096
states, 16384 transitions, and 4096 composed pipe applications/entry. Preparation
may require thousands of commands; there is no additional hop cutoff. Coupled
bounds and the 64 MiB input limit all apply. Exact uint64 values remain integers.

Submit the full `/workspace/project` tree, at most 8 MiB and 256 entries (files
plus directories). All regular auxiliary files/directories are allowed and
collected; symlinks, hard links, devices, sockets, and FIFOs are forbidden.
No extension/name whitelist or extra-file rejection applies. The evaluator
freezes this tree and invokes `python3 -I -B project/campaign_cli.py`. Only this
project is submitted. Do not depend on sibling docs/checker, absolute host paths,
network packages, installed editable packages, or verifier files. The CLI's
bootstrap adds its local src/; no pip installation is needed.

Ordinary nonroot development commands, with all dependencies already present:

```
python3 /workspace/project/campaign_cli.py < /workspace/examples/smoke.input.json
python3 /workspace/public_check.py /workspace/project
```

The public checker runs real bounded children through normal stdin/stdout pipes.
Text, .buffer, fd0/1, fileno, fdopen, and explicitly flushed output before
os._exit(0) work. Empty/non-JSON/wrong/nonzero outputs fail. It is a sanity runner,
not a security boundary; direct root execution is refused. Public fixtures cover
only elementary layout and corpus identity, not the whole domain or maximum scale.
The nonroot public supervisor requires the development overlay documented in
WORKER-PROFILE.md; it restores the scored signal/group denials in each child.
Cleanup of the child's group and adopted descendants precedes acceptance on
normal and abnormal exits. Each fixture retains its120s deadline, plus at most5s
for cleanup; an enclosing controller allows300s for the two-fixture command.

Whole-campaign wall budget is 120s, motivated by offline campaign ingestion and
state-preparation latency. Local limits are 2 GiB address space/process,
180/181s soft/hard CPU per process, 64 processes/threads per leased UID, 256 FDs,
64 MiB/file, initial stack soft 8 MiB/hard unlimited, core dumps zero; stdout
512 MiB, stderr 1 MiB. No task sets CPU affinity. Formal requests 2 CPUs, 2 GiB
memory, no GPU. Runtime CPython 3.11.14, C locale, BLAS/OMP/MKL threads 1.
Python -I ignores PYTHON* environment settings; ordinary pipe buffering applies.

Scored execution uses immutable runtime/project in a nonprivileged chroot;
only /workspace/tmp is writable, cleared per invocation (use TMPDIR). /proc and
host/private task paths are absent. The complete syscall restrictions are in
WORKER-PROFILE.md; sockets/network, namespace/privilege changes, and listed
IPC/process-access syscalls are denied. Ordinary subprocesses/threads are allowed
within limits. Sampled scratch above 1 GiB regular-file size/allocated bytes or
50000 entries aborts as infrastructure error, not a hard storage quota or score.
Formal Docker/layers, cgroups/storage quotas, and transport attestation remain
formal_pending_docker. Local results never manufacture a formal reward.

=== campaign_cli.py ===
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline campaign CLI; JSON stdin/stdout, diagnostics on stderr."""
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "src"))
from eywa.offline import execute

def pairs(items):
    d = {}
    for key, value in items:
        if key in d: raise ValueError("duplicate key")
        d[key] = value
    return d

def main():
    try:
        raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read(64 * 1024 * 1024 + 1)
        if len(raw) > 64 * 1024 * 1024: raise ValueError("input cap")
        def bad(value): raise ValueError("nonfinite")
        def finite(value):
            result = float(value)
            if not math.isfinite(result): raise ValueError("nonfinite")
            return result
        request = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"), object_pairs_hook=pairs, parse_constant=bad, parse_float=finite)
    except (ValueError, UnicodeError, RecursionError):
        result = {"error": "INVALID_INPUT"}
    else:
        result = execute(request)
    json.dump(result, sys.stdout, ensure_ascii=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False)
    sys.stdout.write("\n")
if __name__ == "__main__": main()
=== README ===
# Eywa offline campaign toolkit

The editable package is under src/eywa. campaign_cli.py supplies JSON framing
and adds the local src directory, so no installation is necessary. Run it with
Python 3.11.14. All runtime dependencies are in the standard library.

ast.py defines model types, parameters, expressions and expression evaluation.
oracles.py contains the symbolic type/aggregate visitors and inverse reader.
composer.py owns module dependencies; regex.py owns regular-language objects.
run.py handles corpus identity; state.py prepares stateful replay preambles.
wire.py and offline.py are the incomplete transport/pipeline extension points.
Several existing subsystem assumptions also need repair for the full profile.

The authoritative behavior and output contract are in /workspace/PROTOCOL.md.
All project files may be edited or reorganized. The output certificate is the
interface; private verifier code is never an import dependency.

# Evaluation syscall profile

The local evaluation worker uses a nonprivileged leased UID and a chroot with
immutable CPython/runtime/project. It drops supplementary groups and Linux
capability bounding entries and sets no-new-privileges and non-dumpable status.
No task code sets CPU affinity. Numeric limits and writable paths are specified
in PROTOCOL.md. The worker accepts native Linux x86-64 syscalls only: other
architectures and x32 syscall numbers terminate the process.

The following syscalls return EPERM:

```
socket socketpair connect
shmget shmat shmctl
semget semop semctl semtimedop
msgget msgsnd msgrcv msgctl
kill tkill tgkill ptrace process_vm_readv process_vm_writev
unshare setns mount umount2 pivot_root chroot setsid setpgid
setuid setgid setreuid setregid setresuid setresgid setgroups
open_by_handle_at name_to_handle_at bpf keyctl add_key request_key
perf_event_open userfaultfd io_uring_setup io_uring_enter io_uring_register
pidfd_getfd
```

`clone3` returns ENOSYS. `clone` is rejected with EPERM when its flag argument
intersects `0x7e820000` (namespace creation flags). Other syscalls pass this
filter and remain subject to UID permissions, chroot, and resource limits.
There is no extra no-fork/no-thread filter for this task. Parent cleanup uses
the leased UID and PID handles. `/proc` is not mounted inside the worker.

This is a local development profile sharing the host kernel. Formal container
builds, aggregate cgroups/storage quotas, and submission transport attestation
remain pending. The public checker is a bounded CLI sanity runner; it relies
on its enclosing environment for filesystem/syscall isolation. Running it
directly as root is refused.

## Public development supervisor overlay

The scored syscall list and all scored numeric limits above remain unchanged.
The public checker is a Linux x86-64 nonroot supervisor and needs `kill` and
`setpgid` permitted in its enclosing development profile. Ordinary execution in
the task container permits these. For the offline standard runtime, reproduce
the overlay by removing exactly `kill` and `setpgid` from the enclosing filter's
deny list; retain every other denial and every resource/path/network restriction.
Do not use this supervisor overlay as the direct scored-candidate profile.

The checker calls PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, puts each CLI in a fresh process group,
then stacks a child filter denying kill/tkill/tgkill/setpgid/setsid before exec.
Children inherit the remaining enclosing filter and cannot leave their group.
After normal return, failure, output overflow, deadline, or handled INT/TERM,
the checker kills only that reserved group and reaps its adopted descendants.
Output from ordinary descendant workers remains supported until pipe EOF,
within the same120s deadline, even if the CLI leader has already exited.
It accepts no result until cleanup completes (at most5s additional cleanup).
This uses ctypes/libc, waitid(WNOWAIT), waitpid and killpg from the standard
toolchain; it needs neither os.pidfd_open nor /proc nor third-party packages.
There is no UID-wide signalling or permission to signal another task's processes.

Each public fixture has the unchanged120s wall deadline. The two-fixture command
can take up to250s including cleanup. An enclosing development controller should
allow300s for that command; this does not extend any candidate's120s allowance.
The published command still runs as an ordinary nonroot user. Filesystem and
network isolation remain the responsibility of the enclosing environment.

```python
class PredicateCompiler:
    def __init__(self, types): self.types = types
    def compile(self, node, scope):
        if not isinstance(node, list) or not node: raise ConfigError
        head = node[0]
        if head == 'var': return Var(scope[node[1]], node[1])
        if head == 'const':
            t = self.types.get(node[1]); return Const(t, convert_constant(t, node[2]))
        if head == 'field':
            sub = self.compile(node[1], scope); inner=Type.inner(sub.type)
            return Field(inner.fields[node[2]], sub, node[2])
        if head == 'index':
            sub = self.compile(node[1], scope); inner=Type.inner(sub.type)
            return Index(inner.element_type, sub, node[2])
        if head == 'all':
            binding = node[1]; arr = self.compile(node[2], scope); inner = Type.inner(arr.type)
            inner_scope = dict(scope); inner_scope[binding] = inner.element_type
            body = self.compile(node[3], inner_scope)
            return Forall(Bool(), arr, body, binding)
        if head == 'match':
            sub = self.compile(node[1], scope)
            return Match(Bool(), sub, compile_pattern(node[2]))
        if head == 'not':
            return Not(Bool(), self.compile(node[1], scope))
        op = canonical_op(head)
        if op in BINOPS:
            left = self.compile(node[1], scope); right = self.compile(node[2], scope)
            if op in ('add','sub'):
                t = Type.inner(left.type)
                if not isinstance(t, Int): t = Type.inner(right.type)
                return Binop(t, op, left, right)
            return Binop(Bool(), op, left, right)
        raise ConfigError('unknown expression form')
```

"""Deterministic stateful replay preparation.

A usable preparation is a path of enabled transitions from the initial state
to the recovered desired state, minimising exactly::

    (sum of costs, number of commands, command sequence lexicographically)

Guards are evaluated by the caller on the recovered entry inputs, so this
module only sees which transitions are enabled for one record.  Because every
cost is at least one, every minimum cost path is simple, and the paths of the
"cost tight" subgraph all have exactly ``dist[state]`` cost.  Minimising the
triple therefore reduces to: one Dijkstra on cost, one breadth first pass for
the minimum command count, one reverse breadth first pass from the desired
state, and a greedy walk that always takes the smallest command that still
completes an optimal path.  Forward results are cached per enabled set, so a
replay batch of records that share guards pays for one search.
"""

from collections import deque
from heapq import heappop, heappush

__all__ = ['Preparer', 'BFS', 'MachineGraph', 'INF']

INF = float('inf')
FORWARD_CACHE = 24
PATH_CACHE = 4096


def BFS(transition_dict, target_state, initial="INITIAL"):
    """
    transition_dict: { (state, input) : next_state }
    target_state: state we want to reach

    Returns: list of inputs (commands), or None if unreachable
    """
    queue = deque()
    queue.append((initial, []))
    visited = {initial}
    while queue:
        state, sequence = queue.popleft()
        if state == target_state:
            return sequence
        for (source, command), following in transition_dict.items():
            if source == state and following not in visited:
                visited.add(following)
                queue.append((following, sequence + [command]))
    return None


class MachineGraph(object):
    """Adjacency for a recorded state machine."""

    __slots__ = ('states', 'index', 'initial', 'initial_index', 'out_edges',
                 'in_edges', 'transition_count', 'guard_count', 'guard_slots')

    def __init__(self, states, initial, transitions):
        """``transitions`` is a list of (from, to, cost, command, guard_index).

        ``guard_index`` is ``-1`` for an unguarded transition, otherwise the
        position of the guard inside the per-record enabled mask.
        """
        self.states = list(states)
        self.index = {name: position for position, name in enumerate(self.states)}
        self.initial = initial
        self.initial_index = self.index[initial]
        count = len(self.states)
        self.out_edges = [[] for _ in range(count)]
        self.in_edges = [[] for _ in range(count)]
        guard_slots = 0
        for (source, target, cost, command, guard) in transitions:
            source_index = self.index[source]
            target_index = self.index[target]
            if guard >= guard_slots:
                guard_slots = guard + 1
            edge = (target_index, cost, command, guard)
            self.out_edges[source_index].append(edge)
            self.in_edges[target_index].append(
                (source_index, cost, command, guard))
        self.transition_count = len(transitions)
        self.guard_count = guard_slots

    def preparer(self):
        return Preparer(self)


class Preparer(object):
    """Exact minimum (cost, commands, lexicographic) state preparation."""

    __slots__ = ('machine', 'count', 'initial', 'out_edges', '_forward', '_paths')

    def __init__(self, machine: MachineGraph):
        self.machine = machine
        self.count = len(machine.states)
        self.initial = machine.initial_index
        self.out_edges = machine.out_edges
        self._forward = {}
        self._paths = {}

    # -- caching --------------------------------------------------------
    def prepare(self, mask, target):
        """Return ``(cost, commands)`` for ``target``, or ``None``."""
        key = (mask, target)
        cached = self._paths.get(key)
        if cached is not None:
            return cached
        result = self._prepare(mask, target)
        if len(self._paths) >= PATH_CACHE:
            self._paths.clear()
        self._paths[key] = result
        return result

    def forward(self, mask):
        cached = self._forward.get(mask)
        if cached is not None:
            return cached
        cached = self._search(mask)
        if len(self._forward) >= FORWARD_CACHE:
            self._forward.clear()
        self._forward[mask] = cached
        return cached

    # -- search ---------------------------------------------------------
    def _search(self, mask):
        count = self.count
        dist = [INF] * count
        dist[self.initial] = 0
        heap = [(0, self.initial)]
        out_edges = self.out_edges
        while heap:
            cost, state = heappop(heap)
            if cost != dist[state]:
                continue
            for (target, weight, _command, guard) in out_edges[state]:
                if guard >= 0 and not mask[guard]:
                    continue
                following = cost + weight
                if following < dist[target]:
                    dist[target] = following
                    heappush(heap, (following, target))
        tight_out = [[] for _ in range(count)]
        tight_in = [[] for _ in range(count)]
        for state in range(count):
            cost = dist[state]
            if cost == INF:
                continue
            for (target, weight, command, guard) in out_edges[state]:
                if guard >= 0 and not mask[guard]:
                    continue
                if dist[target] == cost + weight:
                    tight_out[state].append((target, command))
                    tight_in[target].append(state)
        steps = [-1] * count
        steps[self.initial] = 0
        queue = deque([self.initial])
        while queue:
            state = queue.popleft()
            following = steps[state] + 1
            for (target, _command) in tight_out[state]:
                if steps[target] < 0:
                    steps[target] = following
                    queue.append(target)
        return dist, steps, tight_out, tight_in

    def _prepare(self, mask, target):
        dist, steps, tight_out, tight_in = self.forward(mask)
        if dist[target] == INF or steps[target] < 0:
            return None
        total = steps[target]
        if target == self.initial:
            return (0, [])
        back = [-1] * self.count
        back[target] = 0
        queue = deque([target])
        while queue:
            state = queue.popleft()
            following = back[state] + 1
            for predecessor in tight_in[state]:
                if back[predecessor] < 0:
                    back[predecessor] = following
                    queue.append(predecessor)
        commands = []
        state = self.initial
        position = 0
        while state != target:
            best_command = None
            best_target = -1
            for (candidate, command) in tight_out[state]:
                if steps[candidate] != position + 1:
                    continue
                if back[candidate] < 0 or steps[candidate] + back[candidate] != total:
                    continue
                if best_command is None or command < best_command:
                    best_command = command
                    best_target = candidate
            if best_target < 0:
                return None
            commands.append(best_command)
            state = best_target
            position += 1
            if position > total:
                return None
        return (dist[target], commands)

import base64
import json

import sys

CLI = '/workspace/project/campaign_cli.py'


def u32(value):
    return int(value).to_bytes(4, 'big')


def blob(data):
    if isinstance(data, str):
        data = data.encode('latin-1')
    return u32(len(data)) + data


def encode(objects, args=(), symbolic=(0, 0), version=3, magic=b'KTEST',
           trailing=b'', raw_objects=None):
    """objects: iterable of (name, bytes) or dict; preserves given order."""
    out = bytearray()
    out += magic
    out += u32(version)
    out += u32(len(args))
    for argument in args:
        out += blob(argument)
    out += u32(symbolic[0])
    out += u32(symbolic[1])
    if raw_objects is None:
        items = list(objects.items()) if isinstance(objects, dict) else list(objects)
        out += u32(len(items))
        for name, data in items:
            out += blob(name)
            out += blob(data)
    else:

    out += trailing
    return base64.b64encode(bytes(out)).decode('ascii')

"""Independent KTEST builder for fixtures (deliberately not sharing eywa code).

Values are given per protocol JSON representation, except that a string value
is a list of byte values of exactly maxsize entries (so that raw bytes after a
NUL can be recorded), and a char is a one-character string.
"""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/dev')
import kit


def width(bits):
    for candidate in (1, 2, 4, 8):
        if bits <= 8 * candidate:
            return candidate
    raise ValueError(bits)


class Builder(object):
    def __init__(self, types):
        self.types = {t['name']: t for t in types}
        self.number = 0
        self.objects = []

    def reserve(self):
        name = 'x%d' % self.number
        self.number += 1
        return name

    def emit(self, value, width_bytes):
        self.objects.append((self.reserve(), kit.leaf(value, width_bytes)))

    def walk(self, type_name, value):
        t = self.types[type_name]
        kind = t['kind']
        if kind == 'alias':
            return self.walk(t['target'], value)
        if kind == 'void':
            return
        if kind == 'bool':
            self.emit(1 if value else 0, 1)
        elif kind == 'char':
            self.emit(ord(value), 1)
        elif kind == 'int':
            self.emit(value, width(t['bits']))
        elif kind == 'enum':
            self.emit(t['values'].index(value), 4)
        elif kind == 'string':
            self.reserve()
            for byte in value:
                self.emit(byte, 1)
        elif kind == 'array':
            self.reserve()
            for item in value:
                self.walk(t['element'], item)
        elif kind == 'struct':
            self.reserve()
            for (field_name, field_type) in t['fields']:
                self.walk(field_type, value[field_name])
        else:
            raise ValueError(kind)


def build(campaign_types, module, params, result=None, flag=None):
    """module: dict with params/result; params: {name: value}; result: value."""
    builder = Builder(campaign_types)
    for (name, type_name) in module['params']:
        builder.walk(type_name, params[name])
    if result is not None:
        result_type = module['result'][1]
        if {t['name']: t for t in campaign_types}[result_type]['kind'] != 'void':
            builder.walk(result_type, result)
    if flag is not None:
        builder.emit(1 if flag else 0, 1)
    return builder.objects, builder.number

Guards are evaluated by the caller on the recovered entry inputs, so this
module only sees which transitions are enabled for one record.  Every cost is
at least one, hence every minimum cost path is simple and every path of the
"cost tight" subgraph from a state ``u`` costs exactly ``dist[u]``.  Minimising
the triple therefore reduces to:

1. one Dijkstra over ``(cost, commands)`` from the initial state;
2. one reverse breadth first pass over cost-tight edges from the desired state,
   giving the fewest remaining commands from every state;
3. a greedy walk that always takes the smallest command which still completes
   an optimal path (``steps[v] == steps[u] + 1`` and
   ``steps[v] + back[v] == total``).

Forward results are cached per enabled-transition mask, so a replay batch whose
records share guard outcomes pays for a single search.

from collections import deque
from heapq import heappop, heappush

__all__ = ['Preparer', 'BFS', 'MachineGraph', 'INF']

INF = float('inf')
FORWARD_CACHE = 64
PATH_CACHE = 2048


def BFS(transition_dict, target_state, initial="INITIAL"):
    """
    transition_dict: { (state, input) : next_state }
    target_state: state we want to reach

    Returns: list of inputs (commands), or None if unreachable
    """
    queue = deque()
    queue.append((initial, []))
    visited = {initial}
    while queue:
        state, sequence = queue.popleft()
        if state == target_state:
            return sequence
        for (source, command), following in transition_dict.items():
            if source == state and following not in visited:
                visited.add(following)
                queue.append((following, sequence + [command]))
    return None


class MachineGraph(object):
    """Adjacency for a recorded state machine."""

    __slots__ = ('states', 'index', 'initial', 'initial_index', 'out_edges',
                 'in_edges', 'transition_count', 'guard_count')

    def __init__(self, states, initial, transitions):
        """``transitions`` is a list of (from, to, cost, command, guard_index).

        ``guard_index`` is ``-1`` for an unguarded transition, otherwise the
        position of the guard inside the per-record enabled mask.
        """
        self.states = list(states)
        self.index = {name: position for position, name in enumerate(self.states)}
        self.initial = initial
        self.initial_index = self.index[initial]
        count = len(self.states)
        self.out_edges = [[] for _ in range(count)]
        self.in_edges = [[] for _ in range(count)]
        guard_count = 0
        for (source, target, cost, command, guard) in transitions:
            source_index = self.index[source]
            target_index = self.index[target]
            if guard >= guard_count:
                guard_count = guard + 1
            self.out_edges[source_index].append(
                (target_index, cost, command, guard))
            self.in_edges[target_index].append(
                (source_index, cost, command, guard))
        self.transition_count = len(transitions)
        self.guard_count = guard_count

    def preparer(self):
        return Preparer(self)


class Preparer(object):
    """Exact minimum (cost, commands, lexicographic) state preparation."""

    __slots__ = ('machine', 'count', 'initial', 'out_edges', 'in_edges',
                 '_forward', '_paths')

    def __init__(self, machine: MachineGraph):
        self.machine = machine
        self.count = len(machine.states)
        self.initial = machine.initial_index
        self.out_edges = machine.out_edges
        self.in_edges = machine.in_edges
        self._forward = {}
        self._paths = {}

    # -- caching --------------------------------------------------------
    def prepare(self, mask, target):
        """Return ``(cost, commands)`` for ``target``, or ``None``."""
        key = (mask, target)
        cached = self._paths.get(key)
        if cached is not None:
            return cached
        result = self._prepare(mask, target)
        if len(self._paths) >= PATH_CACHE:
            self._paths.clear()
        self._paths[key] = result
        return result

    def forward(self, mask):
        cached = self._forward.get(mask)
        if cached is not None:
            return cached
        cached = self._search(mask)
        if len(self._forward) >= FORWARD_CACHE:
            self._forward.clear()
        self._forward[mask] = cached
        return cached

    # -- search ---------------------------------------------------------
    def _search(self, mask):
        count = self.count
        dist = [INF] * count
        steps = [0] * count
        dist[self.initial] = 0
        heap = [(0, 0, self.initial)]
        push = heappush
        pop = heappop
        out_edges = self.out_edges
        while heap:
            cost, step, state = pop(heap)
            if cost != dist[state] or step != steps[state]:
                continue
            following_step = step + 1
            for (target, weight, _command, guard) in out_edges[state]:
                if guard >= 0 and not mask[guard]:
                    continue
                following = cost + weight
                if following < dist[target] or (
                        following == dist[target] and following_step < steps[target]):
                    dist[target] = following
                    steps[target] = following_step
                    push(heap, (following, following_step, target))
        return dist, steps

    def _prepare(self, mask, target):
        dist, steps = self.forward(mask)
        if dist[target] == INF:
            return None
        if target == self.initial:
            return (0, [])
        total = steps[target]
        count = self.count
        in_edges = self.in_edges
        back = [-1] * count
        back[target] = 0
        queue = deque([target])
        while queue:
            state = queue.popleft()
            following = back[state] + 1
            limit = dist[state]
            for (source, weight, _command, guard) in in_edges[state]:
                if back[source] >= 0:
                    continue
                if guard >= 0 and not mask[guard]:
                    continue
                if dist[source] + weight == limit:
                    back[source] = following
                    queue.append(source)
        out_edges = self.out_edges
        commands = []
        state = self.initial
        position = 0
        while state != target:
            best_command = None
            best_target = -1
            here = dist[state]
            want = position + 1
            for (candidate, weight, command, guard) in out_edges[state]:
                if steps[candidate] != want:
                    continue
                if guard >= 0 and not mask[guard]:
                    continue
                if dist[candidate] != here + weight:
                    continue
                remaining = back[candidate]
                if remaining < 0 or want + remaining != total:
                    continue
                if best_command is None or command < best_command:
                    best_command = command
                    best_target = candidate
            if best_target < 0:
                return None
            commands.append(best_command)
            state = best_target
            position = want
            if position > total:
                return None
        return (dist[target], commands)

"""Strict binary symbolic-test transport (KTEST version 3).

Layout of a decoded payload::

    "KTEST"                       5 ASCII bytes
    uint32  version                 big endian, must be 3
    uint32  argument_count          big endian
    blob    arguments...            uint32 length + bytes, opaque
    uint32  symbolic_argv_count     big endian, bookkeeping only
    uint32  symbolic_argv_length    big endian, bookkeeping only
    uint32  object_count            big endian
    blob    object name / data ...  uint32 length + bytes, count pairs

Every structural uint32 is big endian; recorded leaf values inside the data
blobs are little endian and are interpreted by the harness layout, not here.
No trailing byte is allowed.  Any deviation is a transport error and makes
exactly one run ``INVALID_TEST``.

Object names are returned as the raw recorded bytes.  A canonical name is
``x`` plus a nonnegative decimal integer without leading zeros; the harness
inventory check rejects anything else (including duplicate and composite
identifiers), which is what gives a non canonical or unexpected name its
meaning.  :func:`decode` can additionally canonicalise names itself.
"""

import base64
import binascii
import re
import struct

__all__ = ['TransportError', 'decode', 'object_name', 'MAGIC', 'VERSION']

MAGIC = b'KTEST'
VERSION = 3
MAX_ARGUMENTS = 64
MAX_ARGUMENT_BYTES = 256
MAX_NAME_DIGITS = 12
_CANONICAL = re.compile(rb'x(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)\Z')
_unpack = struct.unpack_from


class TransportError(Exception):
    """A base64 or binary KTEST framing failure."""


def object_name(raw: bytes) -> str:
    """Validate a canonical ``x<nonnegative decimal, no leading zeros>`` name."""
    if not _CANONICAL.match(raw):
        raise TransportError('object name is not canonical')
    if len(raw) - 1 > MAX_NAME_DIGITS:
        raise TransportError('object name is out of range')
    return raw.decode('ascii')


def decode(payload, canonical=False):
    """Decode a KTEST v3 payload into its ``{name_bytes: data}`` mapping.

    ``payload`` may be the recorded base64 text or already decoded bytes.
    Raises :class:`TransportError` (or a base64 error) for malformed input.
    """
    if isinstance(payload, str):
        try:
            payload = base64.b64decode(payload.encode('ascii'), validate=True)
        except (binascii.Error, UnicodeError, ValueError) as exc:
            raise TransportError('invalid base64 payload') from exc
    if not isinstance(payload, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
        raise TransportError('payload is not binary')
    buffer = bytes(payload)
    total = len(buffer)
    unpack = _unpack
    if total < 29 or buffer[:5] != MAGIC:
        raise TransportError('missing KTEST magic')
    (version,) = unpack('>I', buffer, 5)
    if version != VERSION:
        raise TransportError('unsupported KTEST version')
    offset = 9
    (argument_count,) = unpack('>I', buffer, offset)
    offset += 4
    if argument_count > MAX_ARGUMENTS:
        raise TransportError('too many transport arguments')
    for _ in range(argument_count):
        (size,) = unpack('>I', buffer, offset)
        offset += 4
        if size > MAX_ARGUMENT_BYTES:
            raise TransportError('transport argument is too large')
        offset += size
        if offset + 8 > total:
            raise TransportError('truncated argument blob')
    # Symbolic argv bookkeeping is recorded but ignored.
    offset += 8
    (object_count,) = unpack('>I', buffer, offset)
    offset += 4
    objects = {}
    if canonical:
        matcher = _CANONICAL.match
        for _ in range(object_count):
            if offset + 8 > total:
                raise TransportError('truncated object')
            (size,) = unpack('>I', buffer, offset)
            end = offset + 4 + size
            if end + 4 > total:
                raise TransportError('truncated object name')
            name = buffer[offset + 4:end]
            if not matcher(name) or size - 1 > MAX_NAME_DIGITS:
                raise TransportError('object name is not canonical')
            (size,) = unpack('>I', buffer, end)
            offset = end + 4 + size
            if offset > total:
                raise TransportError('truncated object data')
            objects[name] = buffer[end + 4:offset]
    else:
        for _ in range(object_count):
            if offset + 8 > total:
                raise TransportError('truncated object')
            (size,) = unpack('>I', buffer, offset)
            end = offset + 4 + size
            if end + 4 > total:
                raise TransportError('truncated object name')
            name = buffer[offset + 4:end]
            (size,) = unpack('>I', buffer, end)
            offset = end + 4 + size
            if offset > total:
                raise TransportError('truncated object data')
            objects[name] = buffer[end + 4:offset]
    if offset != total:
        raise TransportError('trailing bytes after the KTEST payload')
    if len(objects) != object_count:
        raise TransportError('duplicate symbolic object name')
    return objects

BOOL = {'name': 'Bool', 'kind': 'bool'}
BYTE = {'name': 'Byte', 'kind': 'int', 'bits': 8}


def campaign(types, modules, entries, runs=(), calls=(), pipes=(), machine=None):
    return {'types': types, 'modules': modules, 'calls': list(calls),
            'pipes': list(pipes), 'entries': list(entries), 'machine': machine,
            'runs': list(runs)}


def module(name, params, result, requires=None):
    return {'name': name, 'params': params, 'result': result, 'requires': requires}


class LayoutTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_scalar_numbering_and_widths(self):
        types = [BOOL, BYTE,
                 {'name': 'Wide', 'kind': 'int', 'bits': 33},
                 {'name': 'Colour', 'kind': 'enum', 'values': ['r', 'g']},
                 {'name': 'Ch', 'kind': 'char'}]
        modules = [module('m', [('b', 'Bool'), ('n', 'Wide'), ('c', 'Colour'),
                                ('h', 'Ch')], ('r', 'Byte'))]
        plan = execute(campaign(types, modules, ['m']))['plans'][0]
        self.assertEqual(plan['slots'], [
            ['x0', ['b'], 1], ['x1', ['n'], 8], ['x2', ['c'], 4],
            ['x3', ['h'], 1], ['x4', ['r'], 1]])
        self.assertIsNone(plan['flag'])
        self.assertEqual(plan['variables'], 5)

    def test_aggregate_numbering_paths_and_zero_length(self):
        types = [BOOL, BYTE,
                 {'name': 'Msg', 'kind': 'string', 'maxsize': 2},
                 {'name': 'Zero', 'kind': 'array', 'element': 'Byte', 'size': 0},
                 {'name': 'Nil', 'kind': 'struct', 'fields': []},
                 {'name': 'Pair', 'kind': 'array', 'element': 'Byte', 'size': 2},
                 {'name': 'S', 'kind': 'struct',
                  'fields': [('s', 'Msg'), ('z', 'Zero'), ('n', 'Nil'),
                             ('p', 'Pair')]},
                 {'name': 'A', 'kind': 'alias', 'target': 'S'}]
        modules = [module('m', [('v', 'A')], ('out', 'Nil'))]
        plan = execute(campaign(types, modules, ['m']))['plans'][0]
        self.assertEqual(plan['slots'], [
            ['x2', ['v', 's', 0], 1], ['x3', ['v', 's', 1], 1],
            ['x7', ['v', 'p', 0], 1], ['x8', ['v', 'p', 1], 1]])
        # x0 struct, x1 string buffer, x4 zero length array, x5 empty struct,
        # x6 pair array, x9 the by-value result array identifier.
        self.assertEqual(plan['variables'], 10)
        self.assertEqual(plan['types'], ['Nil', 'S', 'A'])

    def test_void_result_reserves_nothing(self):
        types = [BOOL, BYTE, {'name': 'V', 'kind': 'void'}]
        modules = [module('m', [('a', 'Byte')], ('r', 'V'))]
        plan = execute(campaign(types, modules, ['m']))['plans'][0]
        self.assertEqual(plan['slots'], [['x0', ['a'], 1]])
        self.assertEqual(plan['variables'], 1)

    def test_flag_is_the_final_identifier(self):
        types = [BOOL, BYTE]
        modules = [module('f', [('x', 'Byte')], ('o', 'Bool')),
                   module('m', [('a', 'Byte')], ('r', 'Bool'))]
        pipes = [{'target': 'm', 'filter': 'f', 'bind': {'x': 'a'}}]
        plan = execute(campaign(types, modules, ['m'], pipes=pipes))['plans'][0]
        self.assertEqual(plan['flag'], 'x3')
        self.assertEqual(plan['variables'], 4)
        self.assertEqual(plan['modules'], ['f', 'm'])
        self.assertNotIn(['x3', ['bad_input'], 1], plan['slots'])


class PlanOrderTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_prerequisites_precede_dependents_lexicographically(self):
        types = [BOOL, BYTE]
        names = ['a', 'b', 'c', 'm', 'n', 'z', 'unrelated']
        modules = [module(name, [('u', 'Byte')], ('v', 'Bool')) for name in names]
        calls = [['z', 'b'], ['z', 'a'], ['b', 'c']]
        pipes = [{'target': 'z', 'filter': 'm', 'bind': {'u': 'u'}},
                 {'target': 'm', 'filter': 'n', 'bind': {'u': 'u'}}]
        plans = execute(campaign(types, modules, ['z'], calls=calls,
                                 pipes=pipes))['plans']
        self.assertEqual(plans[0]['modules'], ['a', 'c', 'b', 'n', 'm', 'z'])

    def test_declaration_postorder_once(self):
        types = [BOOL,
                 {'name': 'E', 'kind': 'enum', 'values': ['a', 'b']},
                 {'name': 'Inner', 'kind': 'struct', 'fields': [('e', 'E')]},
                 {'name': 'Outer', 'kind': 'struct',
                  'fields': [('i', 'Inner'), ('e2', 'E')]},
                 {'name': 'Al', 'kind': 'alias', 'target': 'Outer'},
                 {'name': 'Arr', 'kind': 'array', 'element': 'Al', 'size': 2}]
        modules = [module('h', [('x', 'Arr')], ('y', 'Bool')),
                   module('m', [('p', 'E')], ('q', 'Outer'))]
        plans = execute(campaign(types, modules, ['m'],
                                 calls=[['m', 'h']]))['plans']
        self.assertEqual(plans[0]['modules'], ['h', 'm'])
        self.assertEqual(plans[0]['types'],
                         ['E', 'Inner', 'Outer', 'Al'])

    def test_entries_order_and_no_shared_ids(self):
        types = [BOOL, BYTE]
        modules = [module('m1', [('a', 'Byte')], ('r', 'Bool')),
                   module('m2', [('a', 'Byte'), ('b', 'Byte')], ('r', 'Bool'))]
        plans = execute(campaign(types, modules, ['m2', 'm1']))['plans']
        self.assertEqual([plan['entry'] for plan in plans], ['m2', 'm1'])
        self.assertEqual(plans[1]['variables'], 2)


class TransportTests(unittest.TestCase):
    TYPES = [BOOL, BYTE, {'name': 'E', 'kind': 'enum', 'values': ['a', 'b']},
             {'name': 'Nib', 'kind': 'int', 'bits': 4}]
    MODULE = module('m', [('b', 'Bool'), ('n', 'Nib'), ('e', 'E')], ('r', 'Bool'))

    def payload(self, **kwargs):
        objects, count = ktest.build(
            self.TYPES, self.MODULE, {'b': True, 'n': 5, 'e': 'b'}, False)
        self.assertEqual(count, 4)
        return ktest.encode(objects, **kwargs)

    def run_status(self, payload):
        document = campaign(self.TYPES, [self.MODULE], ['m'],
                            runs=[{'entry': 'm', 'ktest': payload}])
        return execute(document)['records'][0]['status']

    def test_valid_record(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_status(self.payload()), 'READY')

    def test_framing_errors(self):
        for payload in (self.payload(magic=b'XTEST'), self.payload(version=4),
                        self.payload(trailing=b'\x00'),
                        self.payload(args=[b'q'] * 65),
                        self.payload(args=[b'q' * 257]),
                        'not base64', '', self.payload()[:-4] + '===='):
            self.assertEqual(self.run_status(payload), 'INVALID_TEST', payload)

    def test_inventory_errors(self):
        good, _ = ktest.build(self.TYPES, self.MODULE,
                              {'b': True, 'n': 5, 'e': 'b'}, False)
        cases = [good[:-1], good + [('x9', b'\x00')], good + [('x0', b'\x01')],
                 [('x00', data) if name == 'x0' else (name, data)
                  for name, data in good],
                 [(name, data + b'\x00') for name, data in good]]
        for objects in cases:
            self.assertEqual(self.run_status(ktest.encode(objects)),
                             'INVALID_TEST')

    def test_composite_identifier_is_unknown(self):
        # x3 is the by-value result identifier of a composite-free harness; a
        # composite identifier can never be recorded.
        types = [BOOL, {'name': 'P', 'kind': 'array', 'element': 'Byte', 'size': 1}]
        mod = module('m', [('p', 'P')], ('r', 'Bool'))
        objects, _ = ktest.build(types, mod, {'p': [7]}, False)
        document = campaign(types, [mod], ['m'], runs=[
            {'entry': 'm', 'ktest': ktest.encode(objects)},
            {'entry': 'm', 'ktest': ktest.encode(objects + [('x0', b'\x00')])}])
        records = execute(document)['records']
        self.assertEqual(records[0]['status'], 'READY')
        self.assertEqual(records[1]['status'], 'INVALID_TEST')

    def test_leaf_range_errors(self):
        good, _ = ktest.build(self.TYPES, self.MODULE,
                              {'b': True, 'n': 5, 'e': 'b'}, False)
        for name, data in [('x0', b'\x02'), ('x1', b'\x10'),
                           ('x2', b'\x02\x00\x00\x00')]:
            objects = [(n, data if n == name else d) for n, d in good]
            self.assertEqual(self.run_status(ktest.encode(objects)),
                             'INVALID_TEST', name)

    def test_missing_object_is_never_repaired(self):
        good, _ = ktest.build(self.TYPES, self.MODULE,
                              {'b': True, 'n': 5, 'e': 'b'}, False)
        objects = [(name, data) for name, data in good if name != 'x1']
        objects.append(('x9', b'\x00'))
        self.assertEqual(self.run_status(ktest.encode(objects)), 'INVALID_TEST')


class PredicateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    TYPES = [BOOL, BYTE,
             {'name': 'Word', 'kind': 'int', 'bits': 16},
             {'name': 'Str', 'kind': 'string', 'maxsize': 5},
             {'name': 'Arr', 'kind': 'array', 'element': 'Byte', 'size': 3},
             {'name': 'S', 'kind': 'struct', 'fields': [('x', 'Byte'),
                                                        ('y', 'Byte')]}]
    PARAMS = [('n', 'Byte'), ('arr', 'Arr'), ('st', 'S'), ('s', 'Str'),
              ('x', 'Byte')]
    VALUES = {'n': 15, 'arr': [1, 2, 3], 'st': {'x': 1, 'y': 2},
              's': [ord('a'), 0, ord('b'), ord('c'), ord('d')], 'x': 9}

    def accepts(self, requires):
        mod = module('m', self.PARAMS, ('r', 'Bool'), requires)
        payload, count = ktest.record(self.TYPES, mod, self.VALUES, True)
        self.assertEqual(count, 12)
        document = campaign(self.TYPES, [mod], ['m'],
                            runs=[{'entry': 'm', 'ktest': payload}])
        result = execute(document)
        self.assertEqual(result['records'][0]['status'] != 'INVALID_TEST', True)
        return result['records'][0]['status'] == 'READY'

    def test_table(self):
        constant = lambda kind, value: ['const', kind, value]
        cases = [
            (['all', 'e', ['var', 'arr'], ['lt', ['var', 'e'],
                                            constant('Byte', 4)]], True),
            (['all', 'e', ['var', 'arr'], ['lt', ['var', 'e'],
                                            constant('Byte', 3)]], False),
            (['not', ['all', 'e', constant('Arr', [0, 0, 0]),
                      ['gt', ['var', 'e'], constant('Byte', 1)]]], True),
            (['and', ['all', 'x', ['var', 'arr'],
                      ['lt', ['var', 'x'], constant('Byte', 4)]],
              ['eq', ['var', 'x'], constant('Byte', 9)]], True),
            (['and', ['all', 'x', ['var', 'arr'],
                      ['lt', ['var', 'x'], constant('Byte', 4)]],
              ['eq', ['var', 'x'], constant('Byte', 3)]], False),
            (['eq', ['add', ['var', 'n'], constant('Byte', 1)],
              constant('Byte', 0)], True),
            (['eq', ['sub', constant('Byte', 0), constant('Byte', 1)],
              constant('Byte', 255)], True),
            (['eq', ['add', constant('Word', 65535), constant('Word', 2)],
              constant('Word', 1)], True),
            (['match', ['var', 's'], 'a'], True),
            (['match', ['var', 's'], 'ab'], False),
            (['match', constant('Str', 'a\u0000bc'), 'a*'], False),
            (['match', constant('Str', 'a\u0000bc'), 'a\u0000bc'], True),
            (['match', constant('Str', ''), ''], True),
            (['match', constant('Str', ''), '[a-z]*'], True),
            (['match', constant('Str', 'a.b'), 'a\\.b'], True),
            (['match', constant('Str', 'axb'), 'a.b'], False),
            (['match', constant('Str', '\u00e9'), '[a-z]'], False),
            (['eq', ['index', ['var', 'arr'], 2], constant('Byte', 3)], True),
            (['lt', ['field', ['var', 'st'], 'x'],
              ['field', ['var', 'st'], 'y']], True),
            (['eq', ['var', 'st'], constant('S', {'x': 1, 'y': 2})], True),
            (['eq', ['var', 'st'], constant('S', {'x': 1, 'y': 3})], False),
            (['implies', constant('Bool', False), constant('Bool', False)], True),
            (['implies', constant('Bool', True), constant('Bool', False)], False),
            (['or', constant('Bool', True),
              ['match', ['var', 's'], 'zz']], True),
            (['eq', constant('Str', 'a\u0000'), constant('Str', 'a')], False),
        ]
        for requires, expected in cases:
            self.assertEqual(self.accepts(requires), expected,
                             json.dumps(requires))


class PipeTests(unittest.TestCase):
    TYPES = [BOOL, BYTE]

    def build(self, pipes, requires=None):
        modules = [
            module('f', [('x', 'Byte')], ('o', 'Bool'),
                   ['lt', ['var', 'x'], ['const', 'Byte', 10]]),
            module('g', [('y', 'Byte')], ('o', 'Bool'),
                   ['gt', ['var', 'y'], ['const', 'Byte', 0]]),
            module('e', [('a', 'Byte'), ('b', 'Byte')], ('r', 'Bool'), requires),
        ]
        return modules

    def statuses(self, pipes, records, requires=None):
        modules = self.build(pipes, requires)
        payloads = [ktest.record(self.TYPES, modules[2], values, True, flag)[0]
                    for values, flag in records]
        document = campaign(self.TYPES, modules, ['e'], pipes=pipes,
                            runs=[{'entry': 'e', 'ktest': payload}
                                  for payload in payloads])
        return [item['status'] for item in execute(document)['records']]

    def test_transitive_applications_and_attestation(self):
        pipes = [{'target': 'e', 'filter': 'f', 'bind': {'x': 'a'}},
                 {'target': 'e', 'filter': 'f', 'bind': {'x': 'b'}},
                 {'target': 'e', 'filter': 'g', 'bind': {'y': 'a'}}]
        self.assertEqual(self.statuses(pipes, [
            ({'a': 5, 'b': 6}, 0), ({'a': 5, 'b': 6}, 1),
            ({'a': 5, 'b': 50}, 1), ({'a': 5, 'b': 50}, 0),
            ({'a': 0, 'b': 5}, 1)]),
            ['READY', 'INVALID_TEST', 'FILTERED', 'INVALID_TEST', 'FILTERED'])

    def test_helper_local_pipes_do_not_attest(self):
        modules = self.build([])
        modules.append(module('h', [('z', 'Byte')], ('o', 'Bool')))
        pipes = [{'target': 'e', 'filter': 'f', 'bind': {'x': 'a'}},
                 {'target': 'h', 'filter': 'f', 'bind': {'x': 'z'}}]
        payload = ktest.record(self.TYPES, modules[2], {'a': 5, 'b': 6}, True, 0)[0]
        document = campaign(self.TYPES, modules, ['e'], pipes=pipes,
                            calls=[['e', 'h']],
                            runs=[{'entry': 'e', 'ktest': payload}])
        result = execute(document)
        self.assertEqual(result['records'][0]['status'], 'READY')
        self.assertEqual(result['plans'][0]['modules'], ['f', 'h', 'e'])

    def test_entry_predicate_filters_even_with_valid_attestation(self):
        pipes = [{'target': 'e', 'filter': 'f', 'bind': {'x': 'a'}}]
        requires = ['gt', ['var', 'b'], ['const', 'Byte', 100]]
        self.assertEqual(self.statuses(pipes, [({'a': 5, 'b': 6}, 0)], requires),
                         ['FILTERED'])


class CorpusTests(unittest.TestCase):
    TYPES = [BOOL, BYTE, {'name': 'Msg', 'kind': 'string', 'maxsize': 4},
             {'name': 'Zero', 'kind': 'array', 'element': 'Byte', 'size': 0},
             {'name': 'Nil', 'kind': 'struct', 'fields': []},
             {'name': 'S', 'kind': 'struct',
              'fields': [('z', 'Zero'), ('n', 'Nil'), ('s', 'Msg')]}]
    MODULE = module('m', [('p', 'S')], ('r', 'Zero'))

    def payload(self, string_bytes, result):
        return ktest.record(self.TYPES, self.MODULE,
                            {'p': {'z': [], 'n': {}, 's': string_bytes}},
                            result)[0]

    def test_identity_ignores_bytes_after_nul_and_model_result(self):
        runs = [{'entry': 'm', 'ktest': self.payload([104, 105, 0, 90], [])},
                {'entry': 'm', 'ktest': self.payload([104, 105, 0, 0], [])},
                {'entry': 'm', 'ktest': self.payload([104, 105, 90, 0], [])}]
        result = execute(campaign(self.TYPES, [self.MODULE], ['m'], runs=runs))
        self.assertEqual([item['status'] for item in result['records']],
                         ['READY', 'DUPLICATE', 'READY'])
        self.assertEqual([item['case'] for item in result['records']], [0, 0, 1])
        self.assertEqual(result['corpus'][0]['inputs'],
                         {'p': {'z': [], 'n': {}, 's': 'hi'}})
        self.assertEqual(result['corpus'][0]['witnesses'], [0, 1])
        self.assertEqual(result['corpus'][1]['witnesses'], [2])
        self.assertEqual(result['corpus'][0]['model_result'] if 'model_result'
                         in result['corpus'][0] else [], [])
        self.assertEqual(result['records'][0]['model_result'], [])

    def test_entries_never_merge(self):
        modules = [module('m1', [('a', 'Byte')], ('r', 'Bool')),
                   module('m2', [('a', 'Byte')], ('r', 'Bool'))]
        payloads = [ktest.record(self.TYPES, item, {'a': 1}, True)[0]
                    for item in modules]
        runs = [{'entry': 'm1', 'ktest': payloads[0]},
                {'entry': 'm2', 'ktest': payloads[1]}]
        result = execute(campaign(self.TYPES, modules, ['m1', 'm2'], runs=runs))
        self.assertEqual([item['case'] for item in result['records']], [0, 1])
        self.assertEqual([row['entry'] for row in result['corpus']],
                         ['m1', 'm2'])


class StateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    TYPES = [BOOL, {'name': 'Msg', 'kind': 'string', 'maxsize': 8},
             {'name': 'St', 'kind': 'enum', 'values': ['S0', 'S1', 'S2', 'S3']}]
    MODULE = module('m', [('st', 'St'), ('msg', 'Msg')], ('r', 'Bool'))
    MACHINE = {
        'states': ['S0', 'S1', 'S2', 'S3'], 'initial': 'S0',
        'state_param': 'st', 'message_param': 'msg',
        'transitions': [
            {'from': 'S0', 'to': 'S1', 'command': 'b', 'cost': 5, 'when': None},
            {'from': 'S0', 'to': 'S1', 'command': 'a', 'cost': 3, 'when': None},
            {'from': 'S1', 'to': 'S2', 'command': 'c', 'cost': 1, 'when': None},
            {'from': 'S0', 'to': 'S2', 'command': 'y', 'cost': 4, 'when': None},
            {'from': 'S0', 'to': 'S2', 'command': 'x', 'cost': 4, 'when': None},
            {'from': 'S2', 'to': 'S3', 'command': 'd', 'cost': 1,
             'when': ['eq', ['var', 'msg'], ['const', 'Msg', 'go']]},
            {'from': 'S3', 'to': 'S0', 'command': 'loop', 'cost': 1,
             'when': None},
        ]}

    def payload(self, state, message):
        raw = [ord(character) for character in message]
        raw += [0] * (8 - len(raw))
        return ktest.record(self.TYPES, self.MODULE,
                            {'st': state, 'msg': raw}, True)[0]

    def test_minimum_cost_commands_and_lexicographic_tie_break(self):
        runs = [{'entry': 'm', 'ktest': self.payload('S0', 'hi')},
                {'entry': 'm', 'ktest': self.payload('S1', 'go')},
                {'entry': 'm', 'ktest': self.payload('S2', 'go')},
                {'entry': 'm', 'ktest': self.payload('S3', 'go')},
                {'entry': 'm', 'ktest': self.payload('S3', 'no')}]
        result = execute(campaign(self.TYPES, [self.MODULE], ['m'], runs=runs,
                                  machine=self.MACHINE))
        self.assertEqual([item['status'] for item in result['records']],
                         ['READY'] * 4 + ['UNREACHABLE'])
        rows = result['corpus']
        self.assertEqual([row['cost'] for row in rows], [0, 3, 4, 5])
        self.assertEqual([row['commands'] for row in rows],
                         [['hi'], ['a', 'go'], ['x', 'go'], ['x', 'd', 'go']])

    def test_preparation_matches_brute_force(self):
        import random
        random.seed(20240501)
        for _ in range(120):
            size = random.randint(1, 6)
            states = ['S%d' % index for index in range(size)]
            edges = []
            used = set()
            for _ in range(random.randint(0, 9)):
                source = random.choice(states)
                command = random.choice('abcd')
                if (source, command) in used:
                    continue
                used.add((source, command))
                edges.append((source, random.choice(states),
                              random.randint(1, 6), command))
            enabled = [random.random() < 0.7 for _ in edges]
            target = random.choice(states)
            graph = MachineGraph(states, 'S0',
                                 [(u, v, c, cmd, -1 if enabled[i] else 0)
                                  for i, (u, v, c, cmd) in enumerate(edges)])
            mask = bytes(1 if flag else 0 for flag in enabled)
            got = graph.preparer().prepare(mask, graph.index[target])
            best = [None]

            def walk(state, cost, commands, seen):
                if state == target:
                    key = (cost, len(commands), tuple(commands))
                    if best[0] is None or key < best[0][0]:
                        best[0] = (key, list(commands))
                    return
                for (source, following, weight, command) in edges:
                    if source != state or following in seen:
                        continue
                    if not enabled[edges.index((source, following, weight,
                                                 command))]:
                        continue
                    walk(following, cost + weight, commands + [command],
                         seen | {following})

            walk('S0', 0, [], {'S0'})
            if best[0] is None:
                self.assertIsNone(got)
            else:
                self.assertIsNotNone(got)
                self.assertEqual(got[0], best[0][0][0])
                self.assertEqual(got[1], best[0][1])

    def test_stateless_campaign(self):
        runs = [{'entry': 'm', 'ktest': self.payload('S0', 'hi')}]
        result = execute(campaign(self.TYPES, [self.MODULE], ['m'], runs=runs))
        self.assertEqual(result['corpus'][0]['cost'], 0)
        self.assertEqual(result['corpus'][0]['commands'], [])


class RegexTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_grammar(self):
        cases = [('', '', True), ('', 'a', False), ('a', 'a', True),
                 ('a|', '', True), ('a|b', 'b', True), ('(ab|c)*d', 'abd', True),
                 ('[a-z]*', 'Hello', False), ('[a-z]*', 'hello', True),
                 ('a**', 'aaa', True), ('[\\-]', '-', True), ('[\\]]', ']', True),
                 ('a.b', 'axb', False), ('a\\.b', 'a.b', True),
                 ('[a-c-]', '-', True), ('[a-c-]', '[', False),
                 ('[a-z]', '\u00e9', False), ('(a*)*b', 'aaab', True),
                 ('(a*)*b', 'aaa', False), ('x[0-9]', 'x7', True),
                 ('x[0-9]', 'x', False), ('*a', '*a', True)]
        for pattern, value, expected in cases:
            self.assertEqual(compile_pattern(pattern).matches(value), expected,
                             (pattern, value))

    def test_long_repetition_is_linear(self):
        matcher = compile_pattern('(a|b)*c')
        self.assertFalse(matcher.matches('a' * 400))
        self.assertTrue(matcher.matches('ab' * 200 + 'c'))


class FramingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    CLI = os.path.join(ROOT, 'campaign_cli.py')

    def run_cli(self, raw):
        process = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, '-I', '-B', self.CLI],
            input=raw if isinstance(raw, bytes) else raw.encode('utf-8'),
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
        self.assertEqual(process.returncode, 0, process.stderr)
        return json.loads(process.stdout.decode('utf-8'))

# Eywa offline campaign toolkit

An offline compiler and replay certificate generator for recorded symbolic
model-testing campaigns. `campaign_cli.py` reads one UTF-8 JSON campaign on
stdin and writes exactly one JSON certificate on stdout; diagnostics go to
stderr and the exit status is always zero.

```
python3 -I -B campaign_cli.py < campaign.json
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .      # bundled regression suite
```

Everything is standard library Python 3.11; no network access, model service,
container runtime or symbolic engine is used. The authoritative behaviour and
output contract live in the campaign protocol document; this tree implements
it end to end.

## Package layout

| module | responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `campaign_cli.py` | JSON framing, strict parsing, `{"error":"INVALID_INPUT"}` |
| `src/eywa/ast.py` | typed model types, predicate AST, scoped evaluation, closure compiler |
| `src/eywa/oracles.py` | symbolic type/aggregate visitors, harness numbering, strict inverse reader |
| `src/eywa/composer.py` | module dependency graph and root-scoped compilation order |
| `src/eywa/regex.py` | regular-language objects, pattern parser, linear-time matcher |
| `src/eywa/wire.py` | strict binary KTEST v3 transport decoding |
| `src/eywa/run.py` | corpus identity and canonical corpus assembly |
| `src/eywa/state.py` | deterministic minimum-cost state preparation |
| `src/eywa/offline.py` | campaign compilation and the replay pipeline |
| `tests/` | regression suite plus an independent KTEST fixture writer |

## Pipeline

1. **Compile** the configuration: named types are resolved lazily and
   canonicalised per declaration name, module signatures are typed, and every
   predicate is compiled once into the expression AST. A predicate that reads
   no variable is folded to a constant; all other predicates are compiled into
   zero-argument closures over a shared environment holder, so one compiled
   predicate is replayed for every record and every composed filter
   application.
2. **Plan** each entry: the module list is the root plus its transitive
   call/pipe prerequisites in Kahn order with the lexicographically smallest
   eligible name; declaration names (enum, struct, alias) follow a
   dependency-before-user postorder over parameters then results; the symbolic
   harness follows the `MainBuilder` numbering convention to produce ordered
   `[object_name, path, byte_width]` slots, the optional final `bad_input`
   flag, and the total reserved identifier count.
3. **Recover** each recorded KTEST strictly: framing, inventory, widths and
   leaf ranges are all checked, and nothing is repaired by skipping to a
   nearby identifier. Values are reassembled through cursor templates, so
   strings stop at their first NUL while every character object is still
   consumed.
4. **Filter**: the flag attests to pipe acceptance only, so it is checked
   before any predicate can filter the record; then the entry predicate and
   every composed filter application decide `FILTERED`.
5. **Prepare** the state preamble: guards are evaluated once per record on the
   recovered entry inputs, and the enabled-transition mask selects a path that
   minimises `(sum of costs, number of commands, command sequence
   lexicographically)` exactly. Forward search results are cached per mask, so
   records sharing guard outcomes share one search.
6. **Assemble** the corpus: identity is `(entry, recovered input values)` with
   JSON type identity preserved; model results are witnesses only. Indices are
   assigned in first usable run order and every usable witness is kept.

## Semantics worth remembering

* Aliases are transparent to values, expressions and harness identifiers, but
  they keep their declaration name in a plan's `types` list.
* A composite reserves an identifier but owns no object; a recorded composite
  identifier is therefore an unknown object and invalidates that test.
* Constants are never truncated or padded, while recovered strings stop at
  their first NUL - so `"a\u0000b"` and a recovered `a, NUL, b` differ.
* `add`/`sub` wrap modulo `2^bits`; `and`/`or`/`implies` short circuit left to
  right; `all` over an empty array is true and its binding shadows lexically.
* Helper `requires` predicates are never evaluated: call dependencies affect
  compilation only, not execution on missing helper arguments.
* Precedence per record: transport/leaf/flag errors, then filtering, then
  reachability, then deduplication.
MDEOF
